主要内容: Companies are increasingly using tax savings to benefit shareholders through share buybacks. In 2018, share buybacks averaged $4.8 billion per day, double the pace from the same period the previous year, according to TrimTabs. This surge follows the U.S. corporate tax rate cut, which reduced the rate from 35% to 21%. J. P. Morgan predicted that share repurchases would total about $800 billion in 2018, a new record. Despite a stock market correction in February, the market rebounded to near record highs in March. Share repurchases have helped stabilize the market, as investors pulled $23.5 billion out of U.S. stock-focused funds. David Santschi, director of liquidity research at TrimTabs, noted that companies are likely using a significant portion of their tax savings to buy back shares. Tax-cut opponents feared companies would prioritize shareholder returns over investment, but recent data suggest both directions are happening. Nonresidential domestic investment increased 6.6% in the fourth quarter, with equipment investment surging 11.8%. Share buybacks have remained elevated even after earnings season ended, indicating companies are using tax savings to repurchase shares.
